briefdescription.para: If we have a shift-by-constant of a bin op (bitwise logic op or add/sub w/ shl) that itself has a shift-by-constant operand with identical opcode, we may be able to convert that into 2 independent shifts followed by the logic op.

detaileddescription.para: This eliminates a use of an intermediate value (reduces dependency chain).

memberdef.argsstring: (unsigned OuterShAmt, bool IsOuterShl, Instruction *InnerShift, InstCombinerImpl &IC, Instruction *CxtI)
memberdef.name: canEvaluateShiftedShift

briefdescription.para: Return true if we can simplify two logical (either left or right) shifts that have constant shift amounts: OuterShift (InnerShift X, C1), C2.

memberdef.argsstring: (Value *V, unsigned NumBits, bool IsLeftShift, InstCombinerImpl &IC, Instruction *CxtI)
memberdef.name: canEvaluateShifted

briefdescription.para: See if we can compute the specified value, but shifted logically to the left or right by some number of bits.

detaileddescription.para: This should return true if the expression can be computed for the same cost as the current expression tree. This is used to eliminate extraneous shifting from things like: C = shl i128 A, 64 D = shl i128 B, 96 E = or i128 C, D F = lshr i128 E, 64 where the client will ask if E can be computed shifted right by 64-bits. If this succeeds, getShiftedValue() will be called to produce the value.
See canEvaluateShiftedShift() for the constraints on these instructions.

memberdef.argsstring: (Value *V, unsigned NumBits, bool isLeftShift, InstCombinerImpl &IC, const DataLayout &DL)
memberdef.name: getShiftedValue

briefdescription.para: When canEvaluateShifted() returns true for an expression, this function inserts the new computation that produces the shifted value.
